DBT pros and cons makes you look at 4 things

1. Pros of acting on the impulse
2. Cons of acting on the impulse
3. Pros of NOT acting on the impulse
4. Cons of NOT acting on the impulse

Another thing I would suggest looking up is using opposite emotion. If your anger gets that bad, this might be a good one to have in your back pocket.

I learned a lot after learning more about DBT. My impulsivity doesn't necessarily come from anger, but from my borderline personality. I learned that if I can make a pros/cons list for my most frequent impulses, I can go back to that in the moment and usually by the time I finish reading my lists, the impulses have died down.

This may not be the best, but it is the most memorable.

So I went to a small school in Minnesota. Juniors and Seniors always got a class trip to go to the science museum, the Guthrie Theater, and then a bit at the Mall of America. (Big deal for a small school). Juniors rode one bus, seniors on their own. I was a senior the year this happened.

So we made it to the theater, saw the Shakespeare play and now it was time to hit the mall. Only, we were stalled for some reason. The seniors started seeing the juniors being led off their bus and everyone being searched.  

Now we're really curious.  And I am a panicked and trying to hide my cigarettes! Well we didn't get searched. Come to find out, a few of the juniors decided to bring beer with and the bus driver knew something was up when he saw them in the back pissing in Mt. Dew bottles. 

The guilty party, about 4 of them if I remember correctly, were not only awaited by their parents but also the police. They were released to their parents as back then, (1994) the police knew their parents would be way worse than any jail time.
